title: Debt and Protocol
premise: Ines Delacroix, a veteran interpreter for a faltering trilateral peace summit, has spent years translating other people's lies while keeping one of their own: knowledge of an off-books arms deal that three governments quietly share. When a burner phone left in their coat pocket rings with the voice of a dead colleague, Ines realizes the 'accident' that killed the delegation's auditor was murder, and the recording on the phone is the proof. Hunted by an assassin working for the deal's architect — Ines's own mentor — and disbelieved by every official channel they approach, Ines finds unlikely refuge with a ragtag crew of delegation staff who become the family they never had. The story ends at the summit's final session, where Ines must choose between protecting their found family by staying silent or detonating their career and nearly their life to put the truth on the record; they speak, the mentor falls, and Ines walks out stripped of everything except the people who stayed.
about_author: Isandro Galloway is the pen name of a former conference interpreter turned novelist who spent a decade in the soundproofed booths of international summits before trading simultaneous translation for slow-burning thrillers. They write from a coastal apartment full of dictionaries, dead languages, and one deeply suspicious cat.

chapters.title: The Packed Bag
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. On the eve of the Meridian Summit, Ines rehearses pleasantries in three languages while checking a go-bag hidden under the hotel bed, establishing their habit of readiness and the polished lie they tell themselves about why. Emotional beat: controlled unease, the calm of someone who has survived by expecting the worst.

chapters.title: Booth Nine
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. During opening plenary sessions, Ines interprets evasive statements from all three delegations and notices the auditor, Tomas Reyes, quietly cross-referencing shipping manifests no one admitted existed. A brief warm exchange with Tomas plants the book's first bond. Emotional beat: professional detachment cracking into curiosity.

chapters.title: A Voice That Should Be Silent
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Returning from a late session, Ines finds a burner phone sewn into their coat lining. It rings: Tomas's voice, pre-recorded, instructing them to listen and then burn it. Before Ines can decide, news breaks — Tomas fell from the twelfth-floor stairwell hours ago. Emotional beat: cold shock, grief weaponized into fear.

chapters.title: What Tomas Knew
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, intercut with a terse scene from the assassin Varga's perspective confirming the kill was ordered. Ines plays the recordings: evidence of a covert arms pipeline funneled through summit logistics contracts, implicating officials in all three governments. Emotional beat: dawning vertigo as the peace process reveals its rotten foundation.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Hand
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ambassador Emeric Vaillant — Ines's former teacher and the man who gave them their career — offers comfort and subtly probes what Tomas may have shared. Ines lies well for the first time in their life and hates how easily it comes. Emotional beat: loyalty curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: junior delegate Amara Okafor and security officer Dov Katz each notice anomalies in the summit's logistics and independently begin pulling threads. Their paths haven't crossed Ines's yet, but the reader sees the net forming around everyone. Emotional beat: institutional dread, competence without power.

chapters.title: Burner Protocol
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Following Tomas's recorded instructions, Ines copies the files to a microdot and hides the original, then discovers the phone receiving new messages — someone else knows it exists. A near-miss with Varga in the hotel garage ends with Ines running. Emotional beat: hunted-animal adrenaline.

chapters.title: The People Who Stay
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Cornered and out of options, Ines breaks cover to Amara and Dov, half-expecting betrayal. Instead Amara offers her apartment, Dov his off-grid contacts. Three strangers over bad coffee become the seed of something like family. Emotional beat: fragile, almost embarrassed trust.

chapters.title: Varga
chapters.summary: Varga's POV. A portrait of the assassin as a consummate professional who begins questioning a contract that keeps expanding — the client now wants witnesses, not just the courier. Varga's methodical world shows its first hairline crack. Emotional beat: chilling calm shadowed by doubt.

chapters.title: Dead Drop Diplomacy
chapters.summary: Dov's POV. The trio attempts to pass the evidence to a trusted journalist through a staged press accreditation, but the journalist is already compromised; the meeting becomes a trap they barely escape, losing the decoy copy. Emotional beat: the cost of trust, paid in blood and burned bridges.

chapters.title: Vaillant's Lesson
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A private dinner with Vaillant becomes a duel conducted entirely in subtext and courtesy; he reveals he knows about the phone without saying so, offering Ines promotion, protection, silence. Ines understands their mentor built the pipeline. Emotional beat: heartbreak disguised as etiquette.

chapters.title: Amara's Ledger
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Working from memory and her own meticulous notes, Amara reconstructs enough of the financial trail to make the evidence legible to outsiders — turning Tomas's raw recordings into a narrative even a hostile commission couldn't ignore. Emotional beat: quiet triumph, the power of patient work.

chapters.title: Safe House Falling
chapters.summary: Varga's POV closing on Ines's. Varga traces Dov's contacts and hits the safe house minutes after the trio evacuates; Dov is wounded covering their escape. Hiding in a shuttered tram depot, the group confronts how much they're willing to lose for strangers. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into commitment.

chapters.title: The Intermediary
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Through an old booth colleague, Ines reaches a neutral-country diplomat willing to hear them — but the price is the original phone, and the intermediary's neutrality is negotiable. Ines hands over a forgery and keeps the truth. Emotional beat: becoming the kind of person the job always demanded.

chapters.title: Countdown to Closure
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. With the summit entering its final 48 hours, Vaillant moves to close the deal early, Varga narrows his search, and the trio realizes the only venue where the evidence can't be suppressed is the closing plenary itself — live, global, uneditable. Emotional beat: converging dread and resolve.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Vaillant makes his final offer: denounce Tomas as unstable and inherit everything, including protection for Amara and Dov. Ines asks for one night to decide — and spends it listening to Tomas's last recording, which names Ines personally as the person he trusted most. Emotional beat: grief and love pulling in opposite directions.

chapters.title: The Long Corridor
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The infiltration plan: Amara forges press credentials, Dov runs interference on security, Ines must reach the interpreters' relay to hijack the closed-circuit feed during the signing ceremony. Every step of the corridor is mapped against Varga's expected position. Emotional beat: taut, breath-held anticipation.

chapters.title: Simultaneous
chapters.summary: Climax, Ines's POV. As the treaty is signed, Ines seizes the relay and broadcasts Tomas's recordings to every screen in the hall — then, when the feed is cut, stands and speaks the truth aloud in all three official languages, untranslatable into silence. Vaillant's composure shatters on camera. Emotional beat: cathartic, terrifying courage.

chapters.title: Varga's Choice
chapters.summary: Varga's POV. Ordered to kill Ines mid-session, Varga instead puts a round through the emergency lighting and walks out, leaving a single line of evidence pointing to his employer. His refusal is the assassin's only apology. Emotional beat: unexpected grace inside a violent man.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Three Languages
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Investigations open in all three capitals; Vaillant, cornered by his own protégé's testimony, chooses disgrace over arrest. Amara, Dov, and Ines give fragmented statements and find they've been assigned a joint protection detail none of them asked to end. Emotional beat: exhausted relief, the strange intimacy of survivors.

chapters.title: The Unpacked Bag
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Weeks later, Ines unpacks the go-bag item by item — passport, cash, the burner phone now inert as a relic — and doesn't repack it. A letter arrives from Varga, unsigned, containing the last missing manifest page. Emotional beat: quiet reckoning, learning to stay.

chapters.title: Debt and Protocol
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, epilogue. At a small tribunal hearing, Ines testifies not as a hero but as a witness, honoring Tomas and refusing to soften the record. Afterwards, Amara and Dov wait outside with terrible coffee and no agenda. Ines finally answers the question they've dodged all book: this is family. Emotional beat: earned peace, loyalty chosen over safety.
